Questo è quello che porti con te. - Come giocatore di squadra, apprezzi lavorare insieme alla pari e contribuire attivamente alla squadra. - Appari aperto, rispettoso e professionale e incontri i clienti con una forte comprensione del servizio. - Possiedi il certificato di ufficiale di polizia federale I e una conoscenza tattica e tecnica approfondita della polizia. - Sei caratterizzato da ottime competenze di tedesco orale e scritto; La conoscenza di una seconda lingua nazionale costituisce titolo preferenziale. - Utilizzi gli strumenti digitali in modo sicuro e responsabile e li utilizzi in modo mirato nelle operazioni quotidiane. ## Il tuo stipendio e i tuoi benefici. descriptionByLocale.en: Police officer: in transport police 50-100% | SBB - - - - - - Move Switzerland with us. Police officer: in Transport Police Olten, from now on or by appointment, 50-100% Apply now ## You can look forward to this. We are looking for several police officers as part of a construction project at the strategically important base in Olten. You will strengthen the existing team and ensure that people feel safe on public transport through community policing. Instead of administrative routine, the focus is on operations close to the action – across cantonal borders and embedded in a strong, appreciative team. Attractive working conditions are important to us – even with irregular working hours. Thanks to clearly regulated rest times and only a few night shifts, work and private life can be easily reconciled at the SBB Transport Police. You can choose your workload flexibly between 40-100%, there is no requirement to have a place of residence. Night and weekend work is paid additionally, e.g. B. with CHF 16 per hour for Sunday work as well as time surcharges of 10-30% for night shifts. Further benefits such as free GA 2nd class, child allowances and discounted travel at home and abroad – you can also find them for your family under “Benefits”. You can move that. - As a police officer in the SBB transport police, you and over 200 colleagues throughout Switzerland ensure safety, peace and order in train stations and public transport from various transport companies. - Your focus is on uniformed patrol services in means of transport, train stations and on the areas of transport companies. - In your role, you make a significant contribution to the safety of travelers and staff in public transport. - During police interventions, you will be responsible for the team and in collaboration with partner organizations - even at major events. - You work in a situation-oriented manner and always have your finger on the pulse of what is happening in public transport. - You will be actively involved in building the team and actively shaping it. This is what you bring with you. - As a team player, you value working together as equals and actively contribute to the team. - You appear open, respectful and professional and meet customers with a strong understanding of service. - You have the federal Police officer certificate I as well as in-depth police tactical and technical knowledge. - You are characterized by very good oral and written German skills; Knowledge of a second national language is an advantage. - You use digital tools safely and responsibly and use them in a targeted manner in everyday operations. ## Your salary and your benefits. We have a fair and progressive wage system and are actively committed to equal pay. Therefore, further and detailed information about the wage system at SBB can be viewed transparently. This position is at requirement level H, regional allowance level 0. More about wages and benefits. ## This gets you started. The fact that you want to move Switzerland with us is our greatest motivation. That's why we don't include a letter of motivation at this point. If you still want to tell us your motivation, you still have the opportunity to do so in our application tool. Doing great things is easier if you do it yourself. This starts with your application. ## This is how it continues. × You will receive initial feedback from us no later than 10 working days after receipt of your application. Final decision up to two months after receipt of application Application Final decision up to two months after receipt of application Any questions? About the application process SBB Recruiting Support Telephone + 41 51 220 20 29 recruiting@sbb.ch #einfachDu FAQ about the application To the position Job ID 102278 Michael Bigler, Head of Olten Support Telephone +41 79 876 95 69 Unfortunately, applications by email cannot be considered. We do not accept dossiers from recruiters for this position. ## This is what we offer. Benefits Benefits Find out more Wherever possible, we rely on flexible working hours and modern working time models. In addition, as an employer, we are also flexible when it comes to balancing your professional life with your private life. Find out more Find out more Differences welcome Differences welcome Find out more With over 150 different professions, we offer an impressive variety of entry and development opportunities. Our employees are just as diverse. That is why we are committed to ensuring that all employees can contribute their individual strengths and ways of thinking. Find out more Find out more Career and development Career and development Find out more We support our employees based on their personal needs and ambitions. To this end, we provide a wide range of cross-disciplinary and cross-departmental training courses. We contribute financially and temporally to selected external further training courses. Officier de police : à la police des transports d'Olten, désormais ou sur rendez-vous, 50-100% Postulez maintenant ## Vous pouvez vous en attendre avec impatience. Nous recherchons plusieurs policiers dans le cadre d'un projet de construction sur la base stratégique d'Olten. Vous renforcerez l'équipe existante et veillerez à ce que les gens se sentent en sécurité dans les transports publics grâce à la police de proximité. Au lieu de la routine administrative, l'accent est mis sur des opérations proches de l'action – au-delà des frontières cantonales et au sein d'une équipe solide et reconnaissante. Des conditions de travail attrayantes sont importantes pour nous, même en cas d'horaires irréguliers. Grâce à des temps de repos clairement réglementés et à quelques équipes de nuit seulement, travail et vie privée peuvent être facilement conciliés à la Police des Transports des CFF. Vous pouvez choisir votre charge de travail de manière flexible entre 40 et 100 %, il n'y a aucune obligation d'avoir un lieu de résidence. Le travail de nuit et de week-end est rémunéré en supplément, par ex. B. avec 16 CHF de l'heure pour le travail du dimanche ainsi que des majorations de temps de 10 à 30 % pour les équipes de nuit. D’autres avantages tels que l’AG 2e classe gratuite, les allocations familiales et les voyages à prix réduits en Suisse et à l’étranger – vous les trouverez également pour votre famille sous « Avantages ». Vous pouvez déplacer cela. - En tant que policier de la police des transports des CFF, vous et plus de 200 collègues dans toute la Suisse veillez à la sécurité, à la tranquillité et à l'ordre dans les gares et les transports publics auprès de différentes entreprises de transport. - Votre attention se porte sur les services de patrouille en uniforme dans les moyens de transport, les gares et sur les zones des entreprises de transport. - Dans votre rôle, vous apportez une contribution significative à la sécurité des voyageurs et du personnel des transports publics. - Lors des interventions policières, vous serez responsable de l'équipe et en collaboration avec les organismes partenaires - même lors d'événements majeurs. - Vous travaillez de manière orientée situation et êtes toujours à l'écoute de ce qui se passe dans les transports publics. - Vous participerez activement à la constitution de l'équipe et à sa formation. C'est ce que vous apportez avec vous. - En tant qu'esprit d'équipe, vous appréciez travailler ensemble sur un pied d'égalité et contribuer activement à l'équipe. - Vous apparaissez ouvert, respectueux et professionnel et rencontrez des clients avec une solide compréhension du service. - Vous possédez le brevet d'officier de la Police fédérale I ainsi que des connaissances tactiques et techniques policières approfondies. - Vous vous caractérisez par de très bonnes compétences en allemand à l'oral et à l'écrit ; La connaissance d'une deuxième langue nationale est un avantage. - Vous utilisez les outils numériques de manière sûre et responsable et les utilisez de manière ciblée dans les opérations quotidiennes. ## Votre salaire et vos avantages sociaux. Rund 14 000 Mitarbeitende des Personenverkehrs sorgen dafür, dass die über 1,4 Mio. Ti aspetta un ambiente di lavoro innovativo, nel quale ti muoverai alle FFS insieme ai tuoi compagni di squadra, oltre a una formazione varia e retribuita. descriptionByLocale.en: Lateral entry train driver: in shunting 60-100% | SBB - - - - - - Move Switzerland with us. Lateral entry train driver: in shunting Brig, by arrangement, 60-100% Apply now ## You can look forward to this. Around 14,000 passenger transport employees ensure that the more than 1.4 million SBB customers we transport every day have easy access to public transport and travel from A to B both safely and on time. As a central professional group, the shunting personnel make a key contribution to this. An innovative working environment awaits you, in which you will move SBB together with your teammates, as well as varied and paid training. You also have various internal training opportunities. Attractive working conditions are important to us, even with irregular working hours. We pay additional wages for night and weekend work - e.g. 16 francs per hour for Sunday work. For night shifts you will receive additional time surcharges of between 10 and 30%. This means you have more free time than employees without night and weekend shifts. Possible training starts in 2026: - May 1st, 2026 - October 1st, 2026 You can make a difference. - You prepare passenger trains for their journey and move them to the correct starting point in and around the station (up to a maximum of 40 km/h). - You put trains together, separate individual cars and make sure that everything is in the right place. - You get the train ready to go, check the most important functions and carry out brake checks. - During your work, you maintain an overview and ensure that all processes run safely and smoothly. - You can repair minor problems yourself or report them to the responsible office. You can find out more about the job profile here. This is what you bring with you. - You are attentive, concentrated and physically resilient in order to successfully complete this demanding work in 24-hour shifts. You also enjoy working outside in any weather. - Since all instructions and documentation are electronic, you will quickly find your way around using digital tools. - You have completed basic education (at least EBA) and already have practical experience - ideally from a craft or logistics environment. - You have good spoken and written knowledge of German (level B2). - You have a perfect sense of color (no red/green weakness) ## Your salary and benefits. We have a fair and progressive wage system and are actively committed to equal pay. Therefore, further and detailed information about the wage system at SBB can be viewed transparently. This position is at requirement level D, regional allowance level No regional allowance. More about pay and benefits. ## This gets you started. The fact that you want to move Switzerland with us is our greatest motivation. That's why we don't include a letter of motivation at this point. If you still want to tell us your motivation, you still have the opportunity to do so in our application tool. Doing great things is easier if you do it yourself. This starts with your application. ## This is how it continues. × You will receive initial feedback from us no later than 10 working days after receipt of your application. Final decision up to one month after receipt of application Application Final decision up to one month after receipt of application Any questions? About the application process SBB Recruiting Support Telephone + 41 51 220 20 29 recruiting@sbb.ch #einfachDu FAQ about the application To the position Job ID 100932 Rémy Tolck, Deputy Training Telephone +41 512 81 98 60 Unfortunately, applications by email cannot be considered. We do not accept dossiers from recruiters for this position. ## This is what we offer. Benefits Benefits Find out more Wherever possible, we rely on flexible working hours and modern working time models. In addition, as an employer, we are also flexible when it comes to balancing your professional life with your private life. Find out more Find out more Differences welcome Differences welcome Find out more With over 150 different professions, we offer an impressive variety of entry and development opportunities. Our employees are just as diverse. That is why we are committed to ensuring that all employees can contribute their individual strengths and ways of thinking. Find out more Find out more Career and development Career and development Find out more We support our employees based on their personal needs and ambitions. To this end, we provide a wide range of cross-disciplinary and cross-departmental training courses. We contribute financially and temporally to selected external further training courses. Lateral entry train driver: in shunting Biel/Bienne, by arrangement, 60-100% Apply now ## You can look forward to this. Around 14,000 passenger transport employees ensure that the more than 1.4 million SBB customers we transport every day have easy access to public transport and travel from A to B both safely and on time. As a central professional group, the shunting personnel make a key contribution to this. An innovative working environment awaits you, in which you will move SBB together with your teammates, as well as varied and paid training. You also have various internal training opportunities. Attractive working conditions are important to us, even with irregular working hours. We pay additional wages for night and weekend work - e.g. 16 francs per hour for Sunday work. For night shifts you will receive additional time surcharges of between 10 and 30%. This means you have more free time than employees without night and weekend shifts. Possible start dates in 2026: - August 1st, 2026 - October 1st, 2026 You can make a difference. - You prepare passenger trains for their journey and move them to the correct starting point in and around the station (up to a maximum of 40 km/h). - You put trains together, separate individual cars and make sure that everything is in the right place. - You get the train ready to go, check the most important functions and carry out brake checks. - During your work, you maintain an overview and ensure that all processes run safely and smoothly. - You can repair minor problems yourself or report them to the responsible office. You can find out more about the job profile here. This is what you bring with you. - You are attentive, concentrated and physically resilient in order to successfully complete this demanding work in 24-hour shifts. You also enjoy working outside in any weather. - Since all instructions and documentation are electronic, you will quickly find your way around using digital tools. - You have completed basic education (at least EBA) and already have practical experience - ideally from a craft or logistics environment. - You have good spoken and written knowledge of German (level B2). - You have a perfect sense of color (no red/green weakness) ## Your salary and benefits. We have a fair and progressive wage system and are actively committed to equal pay. Therefore, further and detailed information about the wage system at SBB can be viewed transparently. This position is at requirement level E, regional allowance level No regional allowance. More about pay and benefits. ## This gets you started. The fact that you want to move Switzerland with us is our greatest motivation. That's why we don't include a letter of motivation at this point. If you still want to tell us your motivation, you still have the opportunity to do so in our application tool. Doing great things is easier if you do it yourself. Als Fachspezialist:in Einsatzleitzentrale der Transportpolizei bist du die erste Anlaufstelle für unsere Kundschaft und das Zugpersonal. Specialist: in the operations control center of the Bern Transport Police, from now on or by appointment, 40-100%, Apply now ## You can look forward to this. As a specialist in the transport police operations control center, you are the first point of contact for our customers and the train staff. With your efforts, you make a significant contribution to safety on trains and stations. Thousands of travelers and employees trust you every day - you are a central factor for peace, order and a safe travel experience. You can move that. - As the first point of contact in the operations control center, you receive emergency calls and reports from customers and train staff, assess the situation and take the necessary steps quickly and reliably. - You support our colleagues at the front by professionally accompanying and coordinating operations throughout Switzerland and maintaining an overview of the situation at all times. - Together with over 190 colleagues in the train stations and on public transport, you make your contribution to safety, peace and order. - In close cooperation with our partner organizations, you will take on responsibility in the security network and help ensure that our customers feel well protected and safe at all times. This is what you bring with you. - Thanks to your service-oriented, open and winning manner, you always treat our customers and train staff in a friendly and professional manner. - Teamwork is important to you – you enjoy working with others and are actively involved in the team. - You will use your good IT and administration skills in a targeted manner in everyday operations. - Ideally, you have the federal police officer I certificate and have in-depth police tactical and technical knowledge, ideally supplemented by experience in an operations center. - You communicate clearly and confidently in German; Good knowledge of French (Level B1) is mandatory and other languages ​​such as Italian or English are a plus. ## Your salary and your benefits. We have a fair and progressive wage system and are actively committed to equal pay. Therefore, further and detailed information about the wage system at SBB can be viewed transparently. Technician:in Safety Systems Interior, Electrical Installer:in, Automatic Engineer:in 60-100% | SBB - - - - - - Move Switzerland with us. Technician:in Safety Systems Interior, Electrical Installer:in, Automatic Engineer:in German-speaking Switzerland, as of now or by appointment, 60-100% Apply now ## You can look forward to that. As a technician: Indoor safety systems, you will independently locate and correct disturbances at our complex systems such as signal boxes and level crossings. You are the one who brings our customers back on track in an instant! Weekly you take over the Picettdienst – and of course there is a fair compensation. In addition, you are responsible for the maintenance, construction and of signalling and control systems. With a well-established team, check not only plants, but the smooth running of Switzerland’s largest transport company. We are looking for support at these locations of German-speaking Switzerland: Lucerne, Brugg, Spreitenbach and Sargans. Attractive working conditions are important to us, even in the case of irregular working hours. You can enjoy the free swimming pools and fitness centers during the week and make your free time more flexible. Night and weekend work is paid for with us. You will also receive time allowances. This means you have more free time than others without night and weekend assignments. Our other benefits such as child allowances, free 2nd class GA and discounted travel abroad - also for the family - can be found on our website under " Benefits". Further insights into the profession as a security system technician: inside you can get at the professional worlds of SBB or directly here: Technician: inside security systems | SBB You can make a difference. - You independently carry out construction and maintenance activities on the signal box interiors and partly on the exteriors. - You actively support the economical guarantee of the reliability, availability and safety of railway infrastructure facilities. During the Picetting Service, you will repair disruptions to the complex facilities to ensure their availability. - Depending on the project, you work occasionally at night and rarely on weekends. You bring that with you. - You are a technically affine personality with an independent and flexible way of working. - Unrestricted hearing and vision is required in order to be able to detect important acoustic and visual signals during track operations. - You have completed basic electrotechnical training EFZ (automatic: in, electrical installer: in or comparable professions). Ideally, you live close to the respective branch, as the willingness to provide weekly piquetting service is a prerequisite for this job. - Readiness to complete the 2-year internal training for technicians: in indoor safety systems. SBB assumes full time and costs for this. - Valid driving licence of category B as well as very good knowledge of German in words and writing at at least B2 level are required. ## Your wages and benefits. We have a fair and progressive wage system and are actively committed to equal pay. Therefore, further and detailed information on the wage system is transparently visible at SBB. This job is in Requirement Level E, Regional Allowance Level 2. ## This is the starting point. The fact that you want to move Switzerland with us is the greatest motivation for us. Therefore, we refrain from a letter of motivation at this point. If you still want to tell us your motivation, you still have the opportunity to do so in our application tool. Making big is easier with you. descriptionByLocale.fr: Technicien : dans les systèmes de sécurité à l'intérieur, électricien : dans, technicien en automatisation : dans 60-100 % | CFF - - - - - - Déménagez en Suisse avec nous. Technicien:en systèmes de sécurité à l'intérieur, électricien:en, technicien en automatisation:en Suisse alémanique, dès maintenant ou sur rendez-vous, 60-100% Postulez maintenant ## Vous pouvez vous attendre à cela avec impatience. En tant que technicien en systèmes de sécurité intérieure, vous localiserez et réparerez de manière autonome les défauts de nos systèmes complexes tels que les postes de signalisation et les passages à niveau. Vous êtes celui qui remettra nos clients sur la bonne voie en un rien de temps ! Vous assumez le service de garde sur une base hebdomadaire - et bien sûr, vous recevez une rémunération équitable en échange. Vous êtes également responsable de la maintenance, de la construction et des systèmes de signalisation et de technologie de contrôle. Avec une équipe bien rodée, vous contrôlez non seulement les systèmes, mais aussi le bon fonctionnement de la plus grande entreprise de transport de Suisse. Nous recherchons du soutien sur ces sites de Suisse alémanique : Lucerne, Brugg, Spreitenbach et Sargans. Des conditions de travail attrayantes sont importantes pour nous, même en cas d'horaires de travail irréguliers. Vous pouvez profiter des piscines et des centres de remise en forme gratuits pendant la semaine et organiser votre temps libre de manière plus flexible. Le travail de nuit et de week-end est rémunéré en supplément. Vous recevrez également des allocations de temps. Cela signifie que vous avez plus de temps libre que les autres sans devoirs de nuit et de week-end. Vous trouverez nos autres avantages tels que les allocations familiales, l'AG de 2e classe gratuite et les voyages à l'étranger à prix réduits - également pour la famille - sur notre site Internet sous « Avantages ». Vous pouvez obtenir de plus amples informations sur le métier de technicien en sécurité intérieure dans les mondes professionnels des CFF ou directement ici: Technicien en sécurité intérieure | CFF Vous pouvez le faire. - Vous réalisez en toute autonomie les activités de construction et de maintenance sur les systèmes de postes de signalisation intérieurs et en partie sur les systèmes extérieurs. - Vous soutenez activement la garantie économique de la fiabilité, de la disponibilité et de la sécurité des systèmes d'infrastructure ferroviaire. - Lors du service d'astreinte, vous dépannez des systèmes complexes pour assurer leur disponibilité. - Selon le projet en question, vous travaillerez occasionnellement la nuit et rarement le week-end. C'est ce que vous apportez avec vous. - Vous êtes une personnalité techniquement compétente avec une manière de travailler indépendante et flexible. - Une audition et une vision sans restriction sont nécessaires pour pouvoir reconnaître les signaux acoustiques et visuels importants lors des opérations dans la zone de la piste. - Vous avez suivi une formation de base en électrotechnique (EFZ) (automaticien, électricien ou professions assimilées). Idéalement, vous habitez à proximité de l'agence concernée, car la volonté d'effectuer un service de garde hebdomadaire est une condition préalable pour ce poste. - Volonté de suivre la formation interne à temps partiel de 2 ans pour devenir technicien en systèmes de sécurité intérieure. Les CFF prennent à leur charge l'intégralité du temps et des coûts. - Un permis de conduire valide de catégorie B et de très bonnes compétences en allemand écrit et parlé au moins de niveau B2 sont requis. ## Votre salaire et vos avantages sociaux. Nous disposons d’un système salarial juste et progressif et nous nous engageons activement en faveur de l’égalité salariale. Des informations complémentaires et détaillées sur le système salarial des CFF peuvent ainsi être consultées en toute transparence. Ce poste est au niveau d'exigence E, niveau d'allocation régionale 2. En savoir plus sur les salaires et les avantages sociaux. ## Cela vous permet de démarrer. Le fait que vous souhaitiez déménager en Suisse avec nous est notre plus grande motivation. C'est pourquoi nous n'incluons pas de lettre de motivation à ce stade. Si vous souhaitez tout de même nous faire part de votre motivation, vous avez toujours la possibilité de le faire dans notre outil de candidature. Du trägst dazu bei, dass unsere Kundinnen und Kunden zuverlässig und pünktlich bedient werden. Auf dich wartet ein spannendes Arbeitsumfeld, in dem du gemeinsam mit deinen Teamkolleginnen und Teamkollegen die Schweiz bewegst.
Attraktive Arbeitsbedingungen sind uns wichtig, deshalb bekommst du auch während deiner Ausbildung den vollen Lohn bezahlt. Nacht- und Wochenendarbeiten werden bei uns zusätzlich vergütet - z.B. mit 6 Franken pro Stunde für Nachtarbeit. Bei Nachteinsätzen erhältst du zudem Zeitzuschläge zwischen 10 und 30%. - Zu deinen täglichen Aufgaben zählt das Kuppeln und Entkuppeln von Lokomotiven und Güterwagen sowie das Durchführen von Bremsproben.
- Du bereitest Güterzüge für die Fahrt vor und sorgst dafür, dass abgestellte Fahrzeuge im Gleisbereich gesichert sind.
- Im Arbeitsalltag nutzt du verschiedene Hilfsmittel wie Funkgeräte und Tablets, um deine Aufgaben effizient zu erledigen.

Ti aspetta un ambiente di lavoro entusiasmante, in cui tu e i tuoi compagni di squadra farete avanzare la Svizzera. Per noi sono importanti condizioni di lavoro attraenti, per questo motivo durante la tua formazione riceverai la retribuzione intera. Paghiamo salari aggiuntivi per il lavoro notturno e nei fine settimana, ad es. 6 franchi l'ora per il lavoro notturno. Per i turni notturni riceverai anche un'indennità compresa tra il 10 e il 30%. Ciò significa che hai più tempo libero rispetto ai dipendenti senza turni notturni e nei fine settimana. descriptionByLocale.en: Lateral entry for shunting employees: in 60-100% | SBB - - - - - - Move Switzerland with us. Lateral entry shunting employee: in Spreitenbach, from now on or by arrangement, 60-100% Apply now ## You can look forward to this. At SBB Cargo you have your finger on the pulse of the Swiss economy. SBB Cargo transports 185,000 tons every day, reducing the burden on the roads by 15,000 truck journeys every day and reducing the burden on the environment by 460,000 tons of CO2 every year. You will help ensure that our customers are served reliably and on time. An exciting working environment awaits you, in which you and your teammates will move Switzerland forward. Attractive working conditions are important to us, which is why you will receive full wages during your training. We pay additional wages for night and weekend work - e.g. 6 francs per hour for night work. For night shifts you will also receive a time allowance of between 10 and 30%. This means you have more free time than employees without night and weekend shifts. You can develop further internally, for example by completing training to become a shunting specialist or shunting train driver. You can move that. - You carry out shunting movements by moving, assembling and dismantling freight trains and wagons. - Your daily tasks include coupling and uncoupling locomotives and freight cars as well as carrying out brake tests. - You prepare freight trains for travel and ensure that parked vehicles in the track area are secured. - In your everyday work, you use various tools such as radios and tablets to complete your tasks efficiently. You can find out more about the job profile here. This is what you bring with you. - Because of your safety awareness, it is natural for you to work according to regulations. - You are physically fit for this demanding 24-hour shift work and enjoy working outside in any weather. - Ideally, you have completed basic training or already have professional experience in crafts, logistics or a comparable area. - You have good oral German skills (at least level B1). - You have a perfect sense of color (no red/green weakness). During the application process, we will require you to provide a current extract from your criminal record and debt collection register (not older than 3 months). The document can be ordered when you are invited to get to know each other in person. ## Your salary and your benefits. We have a fair and progressive wage system and are actively committed to equal pay. Therefore, further and detailed information about the wage system at SBB can be viewed transparently. This position is at requirement level C, regional allowance level 1. More about wages and benefits. ## This gets you started. The fact that you want to move Switzerland with us is our greatest motivation. That's why we don't include a letter of motivation at this point. If you still want to tell us your motivation, you still have the opportunity to do so in our application tool. Doing great things is easier if you do it yourself. This starts with your application. ## This is how it continues. × You will receive initial feedback from us no later than 10 working days after receipt of your application. We do not accept dossiers from recruiters for this position. ## This is what we offer. Benefits Benefits Find out more Wherever possible, we rely on flexible working hours and modern working time models. In addition, as an employer, we are also flexible when it comes to balancing your professional life with your private life. Find out more Find out more Differences welcome Differences welcome Find out more With over 150 different professions, we offer an impressive variety of entry and development opportunities. Our employees are just as diverse. That is why we are committed to ensuring that all employees can contribute their individual strengths and ways of thinking. Employé de manœuvre à entrée latérale : à Spreitenbach, désormais ou sur rendez-vous, 60-100 % Postulez maintenant ## Vous pouvez vous attendre à cela avec impatience. Chez CFF Cargo, vous prenez le pouls de l'économie suisse. CFF Cargo transporte 185 000 tonnes par jour, réduisant ainsi l'impact sur les routes de 15 000 déplacements de camions par jour et l'impact sur l'environnement de 460 000 tonnes de CO2 par an. Vous contribuerez à garantir que nos clients sont servis de manière fiable et à temps. Un environnement de travail passionnant vous attend, dans lequel vous et vos coéquipiers ferez avancer la Suisse. Des conditions de travail attractives sont importantes pour nous, c'est pourquoi vous recevrez l'intégralité de votre salaire pendant votre formation. Nous payons des salaires supplémentaires pour le travail de nuit et de week-end - par ex. 6 francs de l'heure pour le travail de nuit. Pour les quarts de nuit, vous bénéficierez également d'une indemnité de temps comprise entre 10 et 30 %. Cela signifie que vous disposez de plus de temps libre que les employés qui ne travaillent pas de nuit ni de week-end. Vous pouvez vous développer davantage en interne, par exemple en suivant une formation pour devenir spécialiste des manœuvres ou conducteur de train de manœuvre. Vous pouvez déplacer cela. - Vous effectuez des mouvements de manœuvre en déplaçant, montant et démontant des trains de marchandises et des wagons. -
• Vos tâches quotidiennes comprennent l'attelage et le dételage des locomotives et des wagons de marchandises ainsi que la réalisation d'essais de freinage. - Vous préparez les trains de marchandises au déplacement et veillez à la sécurisation des véhicules stationnés dans la zone des voies. - Dans votre travail quotidien, vous utilisez divers outils tels que des radios et des tablettes pour accomplir vos tâches efficacement. ## Darauf kannst du dich freuen.
Bei der SBB hast du die Chance, dein Können einzubringen und dir gleichzeitig neue Fähigkeiten anzueignen, die dich beruflich bereichern und weiterbringen.
Als Bauzugbegleiter:in kannst du einen Grundstein legen für eine weitere Karriere als Lokführer:in Bauzüge.
Du siehst unregelmässige Arbeitszeiten und Schichtarbeit als Vorteil, um deine Freizeit zu geniessen, während andere arbeiten. Nacht- und Wochenendarbeiten werden bei uns zusätzlich vergütet, z.B. mit einem Stundenlohnzusatz von 16 Franken für Sonntagsarbeit. Bei Nachteinsätzen erhältst du Zeitzuschläge von 10 bis 30%, was dir mehr Freizeit ermöglicht.
Benefits wie kostenloses GA, vergünstigtes Reisen im Ausland - auch für die Familie - findest du auf unserer Website unter Benefits und mehr Infos zum Beruf findest du hier
Das kannst du bewegen.
- In dieser abwechslungsreichen Position trägst du dazu bei, dass unsere Bauzüge pünktlich abfahrbereit sind und sicherst damit die Eisenbahnbaulogistik.
- Als Bauzugbegleiter:in übernimmst du die betriebliche und technische Zuguntersuchung und unterstützt den/die Lokführer:in bei sicheren Zugfahrten von A nach B.
- Du begleitest dabei sowohl Rangier- als auch Zugfahrten.
- Nebst deiner Tätigkeit als Bauzugbegleiter:in übernimmst du auf der Baustelle eine Sicherheitsfunktion oder unterstützt deine Kollegen:innen bei Arbeiten im Gleisbereich.
Das bringst du mit.
- Für diese anspruchsvolle Arbeit im 24-Stunden-Schichtbetrieb bist du körperlich und psychisch belastbar und arbeitest gerne bei jedem Wetter draussen.
- Du hast eine Grundbildung abgeschlossen und verfügst idealerweise über eine abgeschlossene Berufslehre. Zudem bringst du bereits Berufserfahrungen im handwerklichen, logistischen oder vergleichbaren Bereich mit.
- Die Weiterbildungen zum Bauzugbegleiter:in (Kat. Ai), Sicherheitswärter:in und oder Sicherheitschef:in hast du erfolgreich abgeschlossen.
- Bei deiner täglichen Arbeit bedienst du unter anderem ein Tablet. Der Umgang mit modernen Arbeitsmitteln bereitet dir keine Mühe.
- In Deutsch bist du fliessend in Wort und Schrift.
- Du verfügst über einen einwandfreien Farbsinn (keine Rot- / Grünschwäche).

## Dein Lohn und deine Benefits.
Wir haben ein faires und fortschrittliches Lohnsystem und setzen uns aktiv für Lohngleichheit ein. Deshalb sind weiterführende und detaillierte Informationen zum Lohnsystem bei der SBB transparent einsehbar. Diese Stelle befindet sich im Anforderungsniveau D, Regionalzulage Stufe 1. Mehr zu Lohn und Benefits .

Dass du mit uns die Schweiz bewegen willst, ist für uns die grösste Motivation. Darum verzichten wir bei dieser Stelle auf ein Motivationsschreiben. Falls du uns deine Motivation dennoch mitteilen möchtest, hast du in unserem Bewerbungstool nach wie vor die Möglichkeit dazu.

Alle FFS avete la possibilità di mettere a frutto le vostre competenze e allo stesso tempo di acquisirne di nuove che arricchiranno e faranno progredire la vostra carriera. In qualità di addetto ai treni edili puoi gettare le basi per un'ulteriore carriera come macchinista dei treni edili. Consideri l'orario di lavoro irregolare e il lavoro a turni come un vantaggio per goderti il ​​tempo libero mentre gli altri lavorano. Per il lavoro notturno e fine settimana paghiamo un salario supplementare, ad esempio per il lavoro domenicale una paga oraria supplementare di 16 franchi. Per i turni notturni ricevi un'indennità dal 10 al 30%, che ti dà più tempo libero. Puoi trovare vantaggi come AG gratuita, viaggi scontati all'estero - anche per la famiglia - sul nostro sito web alla voce Benefit e maggiori informazioni sul lavoro qui. Puoi fare la differenza. - In questa posizione diversificata contribuirai a garantire che i nostri treni da cantiere siano pronti a partire in orario e quindi a garantire la logistica della costruzione ferroviaria. - In qualità di addetto ai treni di cantiere, ti occupi delle ispezioni operative e tecniche dei treni e assisti il ​​macchinista nei viaggi in treno sicuri da A a B. - Accompagni sia le manovre che i viaggi in treno. - Oltre al tuo lavoro come addetto ai treni di costruzione, assumi un ruolo di sicurezza in cantiere o assisti i tuoi colleghi quando lavorano nell'area dei binari. Questo è quello che porti con te. - Sei fisicamente e mentalmente resistente per questo lavoro impegnativo su turni di 24 ore e ti piace lavorare all'aperto con qualsiasi tempo. - Hai completato la formazione di base e idealmente hai completato un apprendistato professionale. Hai anche esperienza professionale nel settore dell'artigianato, della logistica o in settori comparabili. - Hai completato con successo la formazione continua per diventare addetto ai treni edili (Cat. Ai), guardia di sicurezza e/o capo della sicurezza. - Nel tuo lavoro quotidiano usi, tra le altre cose, un tablet. Non devi preoccuparti di utilizzare moderne attrezzature da lavoro. - Parli correntemente il tedesco parlato e scritto. - Hai un perfetto senso del colore (nessuna debolezza nel rosso/verde). ## Il tuo stipendio e i tuoi benefici. Pertanto è possibile visualizzare in modo trasparente ulteriori informazioni dettagliate sul sistema salariale delle FFS. Questa posizione è al livello di requisito D, livello di indennità regionale 1. Maggiori informazioni su salari e benefici. ## Con questo puoi iniziare. Se vuoi ancora comunicarci la tua motivazione, hai ancora la possibilità di farlo nel nostro strumento di candidatura. Fare grandi cose è più facile se lo fai da solo. Inoltre, come datore di lavoro, siamo flessibili anche quando si tratta di conciliare la vostra vita professionale con la vostra vita privata. descriptionByLocale.en: Shunting specialist: in infrastructure 60-100% | SBB - - - - - - Move Switzerland with us. Shunting specialist: in infrastructure Winterthur, March 1st, 2026 or by appointment, 60-100% Apply now ## You can look forward to this. At SBB you have the chance to use your skills and at the same time acquire new skills that will enrich and advance your career. As a construction train attendant, you can lay the foundation for a further career as a construction train driver. You see irregular working hours and shift work as an advantage in order to enjoy your free time while others are working. We pay additional wages for night and weekend work, for example with an additional hourly wage of 16 francs for Sunday work. For night shifts, you receive a time allowance of 10 to 30%, which gives you more free time. You can find benefits such as free GA, discounted travel abroad - also for the family - on our website under Benefits and you can find more information about the job here. You can make a difference. - In this varied position, you will help ensure that our construction trains are ready to leave on time and thus ensure railway construction logistics. - As a construction train attendant, you take on operational and technical train inspections and support the locomotive driver in safe train journeys from A to B. - You accompany both shunting and train journeys. - In addition to your work as a construction train attendant, you take on a safety role on the construction site or support your colleagues when working in the track area. This is what you bring with you. - You are physically and mentally resilient for this demanding work in 24-hour shifts and enjoy working outside in any weather. - You have completed basic training and ideally have completed a vocational apprenticeship. You also have professional experience in crafts, logistics or comparable areas. - You have successfully completed the further training to become a construction train attendant (Cat. Ai), security guard and or head of security. - In your daily work you use, among other things, a tablet. You don't have to worry about using modern work equipment. - You are fluent in spoken and written German. - You have a perfect sense of color (no red/green weakness). ## Your salary and your benefits. We have a fair and progressive wage system and are actively committed to equal pay. Therefore, further and detailed information about the wage system at SBB can be viewed transparently. This position is at requirement level D, regional allowance level 1. More about wages and benefits. ## This gets you started. The fact that you want to move Switzerland with us is our greatest motivation. That's why we don't include a letter of motivation at this point. If you still want to tell us your motivation, you still have the opportunity to do so in our application tool. Doing great things is easier if you do it yourself. ## Darauf kannst du dich freuen.
Es erwartet dich eine 14-monatige bezahlte Teilzeitausbildung zur Zugverkehrsleiterin bzw. zum Zugverkehrsleiter. Nach erfolgreicher Abschlussprüfung trägst du aus der Betriebszentrale am Zürich Flughafen tatkräftig dazu bei, dass 9000 Reise- und 2000 Güterzüge täglich pünktlich und sicher ihr Ziel erreichen. Bereits während der Ausbildung liegt uns deine Work-Life-Balance am Herzen. Deshalb kannst du deine Praxistage für die Ausbildungszeit im 60% Pensum frei wählen und die restlichen Tage somit gut vorzeitig für deine Life-Balance einplanen.

- Du behältst den Überblick über das dir zugeteilte Streckennetz und lenkst die darauf verkehrenden Züge ökologisch.
- Dazu kommunizierst du mit Teamkolleginnen und Teamkollegen, Lokführerinnen und Lokführern sowie Leitstellen und verantwortest die Information für unsere Kundinnen und Kunden an Bahnhöfen.

Responsabile del traffico ferroviario con ingresso laterale (formazione a tempo parziale) Aeroporto di Zurigo, 1 settembre 2026, 60% Candidati ora ## Non vedi l'ora. Puoi aspettarti 14 mesi di formazione part-time retribuita per diventare responsabile del traffico ferroviario. Dopo aver superato con successo l'esame finale, contribuirai attivamente dalla centrale operativa dell'aeroporto di Zurigo a garantire che ogni giorno 9.000 treni passeggeri e 2.000 treni merci arrivino a destinazione in tempo e in sicurezza. Il tuo equilibrio tra lavoro e vita privata è importante per noi durante la tua formazione. Ecco perché puoi scegliere liberamente i tuoi giorni pratici per il periodo di formazione con un carico di lavoro del 60% e pianificare con largo anticipo i giorni rimanenti per il tuo equilibrio di vita. Per noi sono importanti condizioni di lavoro attraenti, anche in caso di orari di lavoro irregolari. Per il lavoro notturno e nel fine settimana paghiamo un salario supplementare, per il lavoro domenicale ad esempio 16 franchi l'ora. Se lavori di notte riceverai anche un'indennità dal 10 al 30%. Ciò significa che hai più tempo libero rispetto ai dipendenti senza turni notturni e nei fine settimana. Puoi spostarlo. - In qualità di responsabile del traffico ferroviario, svolgi un ruolo importante nel buon funzionamento del traffico ferroviario e hai una grande influenza sulla soddisfazione dei clienti. - Tieni traccia della rete di collegamenti che ti è stata assegnata e gestisci i treni che la percorrono in modo ecologico. - Comunicherai con i compagni di squadra, i macchinisti e i centri di controllo e sarai responsabile di fornire informazioni ai nostri clienti nelle stazioni ferroviarie. - Se si verifica un'interruzione, reagire in modo sicuro e rapido per ripristinare il normale funzionamento. - Nel tuo lavoro quotidiano utilizzi un'ampia varietà di sistemi. descriptionByLocale.en: Lateral entry train traffic manager (part-time training) 60% | SBB - - - - - - Move Switzerland with us. Lateral entry train traffic manager (part-time training) Zurich Airport, September 1st, 2026, 60% Apply now ## You can look forward to this. You can expect 14 months of paid part-time training to become a train traffic manager. After successfully completing your final exam, you will actively contribute from the operations center at Zurich Airport to ensuring that 9,000 passenger and 2,000 freight trains reach their destination on time and safely every day. Your work-life balance is important to us during your training. That's why you can freely choose your practical days for the training period with a 60% workload and plan the remaining days well in advance for your life balance. Attractive working conditions are important to us, even with irregular working hours. We pay additional wages for night and weekend work - for example, 16 francs per hour for Sunday work. If you work at night, you will also receive a time allowance of 10 to 30%. This means you have more free time than employees without night and weekend shifts. You can move that. - As a train traffic manager, you play an important role in the smooth running of rail traffic and have a major influence on customer satisfaction. - You keep track of the route network assigned to you and manage the trains running on it ecologically. - You will communicate with teammates, train drivers and control centers and be responsible for providing information to our customers at train stations. - If a disruption occurs, you react safety-oriented and quickly to restore normal operation. - In your daily work you use a wide variety of systems. Accordingly, your work is based on trust in the interaction between people and technology. Find out more about the career profile at the next career information event. This is what you bring with you. - For this demanding work, you are conscientious, reliable, a team player and willing to work 24-hour shifts. - Your networked thinking and your independent way of working help you to react quickly and correctly to disruptions. - You have completed a 3-year vocational apprenticeship or high school diploma. - You are fluent in the language of the training location, both verbally and in writing (level C2) and ideally have knowledge of a second national language (level A1). - You have a perfect sense of color (no red/green weakness). - During the application process, we will require you to provide a current extract from your criminal and debt collection register (not older than 3 months). You can order the documents when you invite us to meet you in person. ## Your salary and your benefits. Classification during the second training is based on function and age. You can find out more about the specific salary for this role under lateral entry. ## This gets you started. The fact that you want to move Switzerland with us is our greatest motivation. That's why we don't include a letter of motivation at this point. If you still want to tell us your motivation, you still have the opportunity to do so in our application tool. Doing great things is easier if you do it yourself. descriptionByLocale.fr: Responsable de la circulation des trains à entrée latérale (formation à temps partiel) 60% | CFF - - - - - - Déménagez en Suisse avec nous. Responsable du trafic ferroviaire à entrée latérale (formation à temps partiel) Aéroport de Zurich, 1er septembre 2026, 60% Postulez maintenant ## Vous pouvez vous attendre à cela avec impatience. Vous pouvez vous attendre à 14 mois de formation rémunérée à temps partiel pour devenir gestionnaire du trafic ferroviaire. Après avoir réussi votre examen final, vous contribuerez activement, depuis le centre opérationnel de l'aéroport de Zurich, à ce que 9 000 trains de passagers et 2 000 trains de marchandises atteignent chaque jour leur destination à temps et en toute sécurité. Votre équilibre travail-vie personnelle est important pour nous pendant votre formation. C'est pourquoi vous pouvez choisir librement vos journées pratiques pour le stage avec une charge de travail de 60% et planifier les jours restants bien à l'avance pour votre équilibre de vie. Des conditions de travail attrayantes sont importantes pour nous, même en cas d'horaires de travail irréguliers. Nous payons un supplément de salaire pour le travail de nuit et de week-end - par exemple 16 francs de l'heure pour le travail du dimanche. Si vous travaillez de nuit, vous bénéficierez également d'une indemnité horaire de 10 à 30 %. Cela signifie que vous disposez de plus de temps libre que les employés qui ne travaillent pas de nuit ni de week-end. Vous pouvez déplacer cela. - En tant que gestionnaire du trafic ferroviaire, vous jouez un rôle important dans le bon déroulement du trafic ferroviaire et avez une influence majeure sur la satisfaction des clients. - Vous suivez le réseau de lignes qui vous est attribué et gérez écologiquement les trains qui y circulent. - Vous communiquerez avec vos coéquipiers, les conducteurs de train et les centres de contrôle et serez responsable de fournir des informations à nos clients dans les gares. - En cas de perturbation, vous réagissez de manière sûre et rapide pour rétablir un fonctionnement normal. - Dans votre travail quotidien, vous utilisez une grande variété de systèmes. Par conséquent, votre travail est basé sur la confiance dans l’interaction entre les personnes et la technologie. Apprenez-en davantage sur le profil de carrière lors du prochain événement d’information sur les carrières. C'est ce que vous apportez avec vous. - Pour ce travail exigeant, vous êtes consciencieux, fiable, avez l'esprit d'équipe et êtes prêt à travailler par quarts de 24 heures. - Votre réflexion en réseau et votre manière de travailler indépendante vous aident à réagir rapidement et correctement aux perturbations. - Vous êtes titulaire d'un apprentissage professionnel de 3 ans ou d'un diplôme d'études secondaires. - Vous maîtrisez couramment la langue du lieu de formation, tant à l'oral qu'à l'écrit (niveau C2) et possédez idéalement la connaissance d'une deuxième langue nationale (niveau A1). - Vous avez un sens parfait de la couleur (pas de faiblesse rouge/vert). - Lors du processus de candidature, nous vous demanderons de fournir un extrait à jour de votre casier judiciaire et des poursuites (datant de moins de 3 mois). Vous pouvez commander les documents lorsque vous nous invitez à vous rencontrer en personne. ## Votre salaire et vos avantages sociaux. La classification lors de la deuxième formation est basée sur la fonction et l'âge. Vous pouvez en savoir plus sur le salaire spécifique pour ce rôle sous entrée latérale. ## Cela vous permet de démarrer. Le fait que vous souhaitiez déménager en Suisse avec nous est notre plus grande motivation. C'est pourquoi nous n'incluons pas de lettre de motivation à ce stade. Si vous souhaitez tout de même nous faire part de votre motivation, vous avez toujours la possibilité de le faire dans notre outil de candidature. Faire de grandes choses est plus facile si vous le faites vous-même. Cela commence par votre candidature. ## C'est comme ça que ça continue. × Vous recevrez un premier retour de notre part au plus tard 10 jours ouvrables après réception de votre candidature. Puoi aspettarti 14 mesi di formazione part-time retribuita per diventare responsabile del traffico ferroviario. Dopo aver superato con successo l'esame finale, contribuirai attivamente dalla centrale operativa di Olten a garantire che 9.000 treni passeggeri e 2.000 treni merci arrivino ogni giorno a destinazione in tempo e in sicurezza. Il tuo equilibrio tra lavoro e vita privata è importante per noi durante la tua formazione. Per noi sono importanti condizioni di lavoro attraenti, anche in caso di orari di lavoro irregolari. Per il lavoro notturno e nel fine settimana paghiamo un salario supplementare, per il lavoro domenicale ad esempio 16 franchi l'ora. Se lavori di notte riceverai anche un'indennità dal 10 al 30%. Ciò significa che hai più tempo libero rispetto ai dipendenti senza turni notturni e nei fine settimana. Puoi spostarlo. - In qualità di responsabile del traffico ferroviario, svolgi un ruolo importante nel buon funzionamento del traffico ferroviario e hai una grande influenza sulla soddisfazione dei clienti. - Tieni traccia della rete di collegamenti che ti è stata assegnata e gestisci i treni che la percorrono in modo ecologico. - Comunicherai con i compagni di squadra, i macchinisti e i centri di controllo e sarai responsabile di fornire informazioni ai nostri clienti nelle stazioni ferroviarie. - Se si verifica un'interruzione, reagire in modo sicuro e rapido per ripristinare il normale funzionamento. - Nel tuo lavoro quotidiano utilizzi un'ampia varietà di sistemi. Completerai la formazione retribuita per diventare responsabile della circolazione ferroviaria, che dura otto mesi e si svolge a Zurigo. Dopo aver superato con successo l'esame finale, lavorerai nel centro operativo dell'aeroporto di Zurigo/stazione di smistamento di Limmattal e contribuirai a garantire che 9.000 treni passeggeri e 2.000 treni merci arrivino a destinazione in tempo e in sicurezza ogni giorno. Per noi sono importanti condizioni di lavoro attraenti, anche in caso di orari di lavoro irregolari. Per il lavoro notturno e nel fine settimana paghiamo un salario supplementare, per il lavoro domenicale ad esempio 16 franchi l'ora. Se lavori di notte riceverai anche un'indennità dal 10 al 30%. Ciò significa che hai più tempo libero rispetto ai dipendenti senza turni notturni e nei fine settimana. Possibile data di inizio: - 1 ottobre 2026 Puoi fare la differenza. - In qualità di responsabile del traffico ferroviario, svolgi un ruolo importante nel buon funzionamento del traffico ferroviario e hai una grande influenza sulla soddisfazione dei clienti. - Tieni traccia della rete di collegamenti che ti è stata assegnata e gestisci i treni che la percorrono in modo ecologico. - Comunicherai con i compagni di squadra, i macchinisti e i centri di controllo e sarai responsabile di fornire informazioni ai nostri clienti nelle stazioni ferroviarie. - Se si verifica un'interruzione, reagire in modo sicuro e rapido per ripristinare il normale funzionamento. - Nel tuo lavoro quotidiano utilizzi un'ampia varietà di sistemi. Di conseguenza, il tuo lavoro si basa sulla fiducia nell’interazione tra persone e tecnologia. Scopri di più sul profilo professionale al nostro prossimo evento informativo sulla carriera. Lateral entry train traffic manager: in 2026 Zurich Airport or Limmattal marshalling yard, by arrangement, 100% Apply now ## You can look forward to this. You will complete paid training to become a train traffic manager, which lasts eight months and is carried out in Zurich. After successfully completing your final exam, you will work in the Zurich Airport operations center / Limmattal marshalling yard and help ensure that 9,000 passenger and 2,000 freight trains reach their destination on time and safely every day. Attractive working conditions are important to us, even with irregular working hours. We pay additional wages for night and weekend work - for example, 16 francs per hour for Sunday work. If you work at night, you will also receive a time allowance of 10 to 30%. This means you have more free time than employees without night and weekend shifts. Possible start date: - October 1st, 2026 You can make a difference. - As a train traffic manager, you play an important role in the smooth running of rail traffic and have a major influence on customer satisfaction. - You keep track of the route network assigned to you and manage the trains running on it ecologically. - You will communicate with teammates, train drivers and control centers and be responsible for providing information to our customers at train stations. - If a disruption occurs, you react safety-oriented and quickly to restore normal operation. - In your daily work you use a wide variety of systems. Accordingly, your work is based on trust in the interaction between people and technology. Find out more about the career profile at our next career information event. This is what you bring with you. - For this demanding work, you are conscientious, reliable, a team player and willing to work 24-hour shifts. - Your networked thinking and your independent way of working help you to react quickly and correctly to disruptions. - You have completed a 3-year vocational apprenticeship or high school diploma. - You are fluent in the language of the training location, both verbally and in writing (level C2). - You have a perfect sense of color (no red/green weakness). - During the application process, we will require you to provide a current extract from your criminal record and debt collection register (not older than 3 months). The document can be ordered when you are invited to get to know each other in person. ## Your salary and your benefits. Classification during the second training is based on function and age. You can find out more about the specific salary for this role under lateral entry. ## This gets you started. The fact that you want to move Switzerland with us is our greatest motivation. Après avoir réussi votre examen final, vous travaillerez au centre opérationnel de l'aéroport de Zurich / gare de triage de Limmattal et contribuerez à ce que 9 000 trains de passagers et 2 000 trains de marchandises arrivent chaque jour à temps et en toute sécurité à destination. Around 14,000 passenger transport employees ensure that the more than 1.3 million customers SBB transports daily have easy access to public transport and travel safely and punctually from A to B. As a central professional group, shunting personnel make a key contribution to this. An innovative working environment awaits you, where you will move SBB together with your team colleagues. In addition, you have various internal further training opportunities, such as training to become a shunting locomotive driver. Attractive working conditions are important to us, even with irregular working hours. Night and weekend work is additionally remunerated - e.g., with 16 francs per hour for Sunday work. For night shifts, you also receive time supplements between 10 and 30%. This means you have more free time than employees without night and weekend shifts. What you can move. - As a shunting specialist, you contribute to our customers traveling reliably and punctually by moving, forming, and dismantling passenger trains according to the train formation plan. - You lead individual shunting movements and return train compositions. - Your responsibility for train preparation includes preheating and air-conditioning the trains as well as performing train inspections and brake tests. - You report irregularities, special incidents, or deviations to the responsible office. - Due to your safety awareness, it is a matter of course for you to work according to regulations. Find out more about the job profile here.
• What you bring with you. - You are already a trained shunting specialist Ai40. - You are attentive, focused, and physically resilient to successfully cope with this demanding work in 24-hour shift operation. Furthermore, you enjoy working outside in any weather. - Since all instructions and documentation are electronic, you will quickly find your way around with digital tools. - You are fluent in German (level C2). - You have perfect color vision (no red-green deficiency). Therefore, further and detailed information on the salary system at SBB is transparently viewable. This position is in requirement level D, regional allowance level 0. More about salary and benefits. Shunting specialist: in Ai40 Zurich, from now on or by appointment, 60-100% Apply now You can look forward to this. Around 14,000 passenger transport employees ensure that the more than 1.3 million SBB customers we transport every day have easy access to public transport and travel from A to B both safely and on time. As a central professional group, the shunting personnel make a key contribution to this. An innovative working environment awaits you, in which you will move SBB together with your teammates, as well as varied and paid training. You also have various internal training opportunities, such as training to become a shunting engine driver. Attractive working conditions are important to us, even with irregular working hours. We pay additional wages for night and weekend work - e.g. 16 francs per hour for Sunday work. For night shifts you will receive additional time surcharges of between 10 and 30%. This means you have more free time than employees without night and weekend shifts. You can move that. - As a shunting specialist, you will help ensure that our customers travel reliably and on time by moving, forming and dismantling passenger trains according to the train formation plan. - You lead individual shunting movements and reset train compositions. - Your responsibility for train preparation includes preheating and air conditioning the trains as well as carrying out train inspections and brake tests. - You report any irregularities, special incidents or deviations to the responsible authority. - Due to your safety awareness, it is natural for you to work according to regulations. You can find out more about the job profile here. This is what you bring with you. - You are attentive, concentrated and physically resilient in order to successfully complete this demanding work in 24-hour shifts. You also enjoy working outside in any weather. - You are already a trained shunting specialist in Ai40. - Since all instructions and documentation are electronic, you will quickly find your way around using digital tools. - You are fluent in German (level C2). - You have a perfect sense of color (no red-green weakness). Your salary and your benefits. We have a fair and progressive wage system and are actively committed to equal pay. Therefore, further and detailed information about the wage system at SBB can be viewed transparently. This position is at requirement level D, regional allowance level 2. ## Darauf kannst du dich freuen.
Auf dich wartet eine abwechslungsreiche, bezahlte 9-monatige Vollzeitausbildung. Die theoretische Ausbildung absolvierst du in Olten und deine ersten Praxiserfahrungen sammelst du in einem regional zugeteilten Rangierbahnhof.
Du siehst unregelmässige Arbeitszeiten und Schichtarbeit als Vorteil, um deine Freizeit zu geniessen, während andere arbeiten. Nacht- und Wochenendarbeiten werden bei uns zusätzlich vergütet, z.B. mit einem Stundenlohnzusatz von 16 Franken für Sonntagsarbeit. Bei Nachteinsätzen erhältst du Zeitzuschläge von 10 bis 30%, was dir mehr Freizeit ermöglicht.
Benefits wie kostenloses GA, vergünstigtes Reisen im Ausland - auch für die Familie - findest du auf unserer Website unter Benefits und mehr Infos zum Beruf findest du hier.
Das kannst du bewegen.
- Als Lokführerin oder Lokführer Bauzüge leistest du einen grossen Beitrag, um die Erneuerungen der Trassen (Gleise, Schotter usw.) sicherzustellen.
- Du leistest und führst verschiedene und komplexe Rangierbewegungen von Zügen bis zu maximal 100 km/h selbständig, formierst und zerlegst diese und bereitest sie für die Fahrt vor.
- Um die regionale Logistik sicherzustellen, entwirfst, beantragst und bestellst du Fahrordnungen termingerecht und verantwortest die Versorgung von Baustellen mit den erforderlichen Materialien.
- Du hast eine hohe Verantwortung in der Betriebssicherheit der Bauzüge. Das Prüfen der Arbeitsstellensicherheit sowie Erstellen von Rapporten runden die Tätigkeiten ab.
- Zusätzlich wirst du als Lokführerinnen und Lokführer Bauzüge auf der Baustelle eingesetzt und dein handwerkliches Geschick wird gefordert.
Das bringst du mit.
- Für diese anspruchsvolle Arbeit bist du gewissenhaft, zuverlässig, teamfähig und bereit im 24 Stunden Schichtbetrieb zu arbeiten.
- Du bist körperlich und psychisch belastbar und kannst mit deiner eigenverantwortlichen Arbeitsweise bewusst und richtig agieren.
- Du hast eine mindestens zweijährige anerkannte Berufslehre inkl. Fähigkeitsausweis, idealerweise in der Baubranche und mit Erfahrungen im Gleisbau oder abgeschlossene Matura.
- Fliessende Deutschkenntnisse (Niveau C1) in Wort und Schrift sind Voraussetzung.
- Du besitzt den Führerausweis Kategorie B.
- Du verfügst über einen einwandfreien Farbsinn (keine Rot- / Grünschwäche) und weist keine Einträge im Straf- und Betreibungsregister auf.

## Dein Lohn und deine Benefits.
Die Einstufung während der Zweitausbildung erfolgt entsprechend der Funktion und dem Alter. Mehr zum konkreten Lohn für diese Rolle findest du unter Quereinstieg .

Dass du mit uns die Schweiz bewegen willst, ist für uns die grösste Motivation. Darum verzichten wir bei dieser Stelle auf ein Motivationsschreiben. Falls du uns deine Motivation dennoch mitteilen möchtest, hast du in unserem Bewerbungstool nach wie vor die Möglichkeit dazu.
Grosses machen ist einfacher per du. Das beginnt bereits bei deiner Bewerbung.
